properties.state: {"concern":"core","designation":"internal","kind":"functional","lineage":"original","name":"Friction is classified and has a bar at which it becomes work","priority":"medium","provenance":"authored","statement":"reflow2 collects friction with no vocabulary for it and no threshold at which accumulated friction becomes scheduled work, so reports pile up and nothing converts them. THE EVIDENCE IS IN THIS REPO, twice over. (1) The eight brainmaker friction items in feedback.md — from a real genesis pass over a 47-component decomposition — are still not in docs/backlog.md. Observed, written down, and never converted. (2) Friction findings with nowhere to live are being crammed into node NAMES: ver:kit-manifest-agrees is literally named \"... (friction 2026-07-25: reflow2's own manifest is four releases stale and nothing noticed; unwritten)\" and ver:tools-reject-unknown-args carries \"(friction 2026-07-25, unwritten)\". When a finding has no home it ends up in a name string, and \"unwritten\" in a Verification name is a backlog entry in hiding. THE PRIOR ART, from reflow's 97-GAN-inspired-test.json: friction was classified into a fixed taxonomy of twelve categories — tool_workflow_misalignment (tool output does not match the documentation), missing_documentation, automation_incompatibility (requires human interaction, fails unattended), missing_tools (workflow references something that does not exist), ambiguous_instructions, template_issues, path_resolution_issues, plus five for the hierarchical machinery. Each finding was prioritised against stated criteria rather than judgement: P0 BLOCKING, \"workflow cannot proceed without manual intervention or workaround\"; P1 HIGH VALUE, \"causes significant friction (5+ minutes wasted) or happens frequently\"; P2 POLISH. And there was a bar: p0_issues_count > 0 OR (p1_issues_count > 3 AND friction_overhead > 15%) converted the pile into a fix cycle. The specific numbers are reflow's and are not the point; the point is that a stated bar exists, so friction stops depending on someone feeling that there is enough of it. NOTE WHAT reflow2 ALREADY DOES BETTER and must keep: report-friction's redaction discipline (tool names and argument SHAPES, node TYPES not ids, counts not contents, errors with ids masked) has no counterpart in reflow's loop, because reflow's ran on its own repo where there was no third party's design to protect. reflow2 installs once per machine into other people's projects, so any classification scheme must carry that discipline with it. Found 2026-07-28 reviewing the original reflow workflows. Anthony's word: capture it.","status":"proposed"}
